observation.visible_scene: A male performer stands on a stage lit in deep blue, positioned on a patterned rug in front of a microphone on a stand. He holds an electric guitar with a yellow headstock, wearing a black t-shirt and dark jeans. A bright white stage light glows at the left, and a grid of small white lights is visible in the dark background on the right. The back of another person's head occupies the left foreground in much of the clip.
visible_changes: The guitarist's right hand moves repeatedly up and down over the strings near the guitar body throughout the segment, consistent with continuous strumming/picking.

The performer's head posture changes: he looks forward/up at the start, tilts downward toward the guitar through the middle frames, then lifts back up toward the microphone, with his mouth opening near the mic in the later frames as if singing.

A foreground head at the left edge grows progressively more prominent across the frames while the background light grid shifts position, indicating a slow camera pan/viewpoint drift rather than motion of the guitarist himself.
The guitarist's left hand stays on the neck, with small positional adjustments along the fretboard.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the singing begins exactly at this point or was already ongoing before the crop.
The cause of the camera's lateral shift and what lies beyond the frame edges.
Any audio content or the full song structure.
uncertain_details: Whether the foreground head's increased visibility is due to camera movement or the person leaning/moving; background parallax suggests camera pan but is not definitive.
Exact nature of the head-down phase (looking at guitar vs. brief rest).
